entities.summary: Franchinus Gaffurius was a renowned Italian music theorist and composer of the Renaissance, born around 1466 in Padua, Italy, and died on July 5, 1522. He was a key figure in the development of Western classical music, and his treatise 'De Harmonia Instrumentali' (1500) remains a foundational work in the field. Gaffurius's contributions to music theory and composition had a lasting impact on the evolution of Western classical music, influencing prominent composers such as Palestrina and Lasso. His work also reflects the cultural and artistic achievements of the Italian Renaissance, a period marked by significant advancements in art, literature, and science. The legacy of Franchinus Gaffurius continues to be celebrated by musicologists and scholars of the Renaissance, who recognize his innovative approach to music theory and his enduring influence on the development of Western classical music.
